title: Fatemeh Monshizadeh
text:
I am currently a PhD student at Cardiff University, UK, specializing in Digital Twins, Industry 4.0, Healthcare, and Digital Business Models. My research focuses on exploring the transformative potential of Digital Twins in healthcare, including their applications, challenges, and benefits.
With a strong academic foundation and hands-on research experience, I am eager to bring my expertise to businesses, particularly in management consulting and digital transformation. I am passionate about helping organizations leverage cutting-edge technologies to optimize operations, enhance decision-making, and drive innovation.
As a self-motivated and driven individual, I thrive in dynamic environments where creativity, collaboration, and effective communication can make a meaningful impact. My goal is to bridge the gap between academic insights and practical applications, empowering businesses to adapt and excel in the digital age.
Explore my full list of publications on Google Scholar.

title: First Post
text:
🎯 How can the healthcare ecosystem be transformed beyond just applying new technologies?
As part of my PhD research on DigitalTwins in Healthcare, I recently read a compelling book, “Digital Transformation in Healthcare: An Ecosystem Approach”, by Prof. Panos Constantinides, which has shaped my thinking on this question.
The book explores the complexities of digital_evolution in healthcare, highlighting several systemic challenges:
📌 Rising service costs 📌 Unclear benefits 📌 Fragmented data access and interoperability issues 📌 Siloed infrastructures and coordination challenges
These are not merely technical problems; they are structural and relational, rooted in the interconnected network of stakeholders within the healthcare ecosystem. The book emphasizes the importance of co-adoption and co-innovation to create sustainable and value-driven partnerships.
From my PhD perspective, digital twins offer an integrative approach to these challenges, leveraging real-time simulation, predictive modeling, and data harmonization to generate actionable insights, enhance coordination, and support system-wide innovation.
This book has deepened my understanding of what true digital transformation in healthcare requires:
➡️ A shift in mindset ➡️ A focus on ecosystem_wide collaboration ➡️ A rethinking of relationships, responsibilities, and value_creation.

title: Who am I
text:
I am Fatemeh Monshizadeh, a PhD candidate at Cardiff Business School (Data Lab for Social Good). My research focuses on developing a digital twin model for healthcare, aiming to offer personalized treatment to patients by leveraging the benefits of the digital twin concept.
With a strong academic foundation and hands-on research experience, I am passionate about helping organizations harness advanced technologies to optimize operations, enhance decision-making, and drive innovation. My expertise lies in bridging academic insights with real-world applications, empowering businesses to adapt and thrive in an increasingly digital world. Alongside my PhD work, I am responsible for managing social media at the Data Lab for Social Good.

title: Who am I
text:
Research focus / PhD project
My research focuses on advancing the development and application of digital twins in healthcare, with a particular emphasis on improving clinical decision-making, operational efficiency, and patient outcomes. Despite the transformative potential of digital twins, their adoption in healthcare is hindered by challenges such as data heterogeneity, integration complexity, ethical concerns, and uncertainties in clinical environments. By combining simulation modelling, machine learning, and stakeholder theory, my work aims to develop conceptual and computational models that can support real-time decision-making and enhance the reliability of digital twin systems—especially in high-risk domains such as cancer care and emergency response.
This interdisciplinary project brings together expertise from Cardiff Business School, the School of Computer Science & Informatics, and clinical partners. It involves analysing the benefits, risks, and challenges of digital twins across different levels of the healthcare ecosystem (micro, meso, and macro), developing taxonomies of modelling techniques, and exploring the roadmap for safe and responsible implementation. Ultimately, my research aims to support clinicians, patients, healthcare managers, and policymakers by providing evidence-based frameworks that guide the development of trustworthy digital twins, improving quality of care, resource efficiency, and system resilience.
